metadata.title: Piper Sandler Makes Blunt Call on Two Nuclear Stocks

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Piper Sandler has drawn a sharp dividing line through the advanced nuclear sector, naming Oklo (NYSE:OKLO) its preferred bet while warning that Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN)-backed X-Energy (NASDAQ:XE) could lose more than half its value.
Analyst Dimple Gosai initiated Oklo (NYSE:OKLO) with a Buy rating and $55 price target, implying roughly 27% upside from about $43. She described its business model as bankable by design, arguing that the structure can make projects easier to finance and customers easier to secure.
The contrast was severe. Gosai started coverage of X-Energy (NASDAQ:XE) with a Sell rating and $9 target, representing approximately 53% downside from Tuesday's $19.15 close.
Why Piper Sandler Prefers Oklo Stock
Oklo (NYSE:OKLO) is developing the Aurora Powerhouse, a fast reactor cooled by liquid sodium instead of water. The design avoids the high-pressure steam systems used by conventional water-cooled reactors and is intended to operate for longer periods.
The investment thesis extends beyond the reactor. Oklo (NYSE:OKLO) plans to finance, build, own and operate its plants, then sell electricity to customers. Buyers can access nuclear power without becoming developers or assuming direct responsibility for deploying unfamiliar reactor technology.
X-Energy (NASDAQ:XE), by comparison, follows a more asset-light approach that leaves customers carrying more technology and project risk, according to Gosai. That difference drives Piper Sandler's opposing ratings.
Gosai estimates Oklo's (NYSE:OKLO) first 75-megawatt plants could produce a 6.5% unlevered internal rate of return. Repeating the design and construction process could lift that return to 13%. At scale, she projects EBITDA margins near 60%, compared with midteen margins for equipment-focused rivals.
Execution risk remains considerable. Oklo (NYSE:OKLO) must finance, license, construct and operate first-of-a-kind plants before those economics can be demonstrated for investors. Yet Wall Street remains constructive, with eight Buy ratings and seven Holds. Its $72.95 consensus target implies approximately 69% upside, substantially exceeding Piper Sandler's more conservative forecast.
